thread:
ashley: Heads-up — after rolling cuda-toolkit:12.0 to the us-west pool a subset of nodes started failing runtime loads. Containers OOM'd during model warmup and NCCL timeouts spiked. Pulling in @oncall-bot
kevin: seeing same, metrics show PTX compile spikes and heavy disk write from ptx cache at /var/lib/nv/ptxcache
andre: can you paste logs? especially ld.so errors
ashley: paste logs snippet
```
stderr: /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12: version `CUDART_12_0' not found
E  cuda_driver: failed to load kernel module: modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found
NCCL INFO ... timeout waiting for rank
```
andre: looks like image built against GCC 13 but node has host driver toolchain expecting libstdc++ from gcc11 — JIT can't link PTX -> falls back, OOMs
jia: how many nodes affected? any evictions? cost impact?
kevin: ~18 nodes in us-west-1a/1b; 120 running pods affected; eviction rate ~0.8 pods/min during ptx cache rebuilds; provisioner temporarily launched extra instances but they also hit same image
sre-rotations: flagged for oncall, initiating canary rollback
oncall-bot: @ashley assigned to oncall rotation — paging
deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-18T12:04Z rolled cuda-toolkit:12.0 to us-west
andre: if rebuild containers are writing PTX cache to ephemeral local SSDs we're saturating IO. option: mount ptx cache on tmpfs to avoid heavy writes (short term) or pre-warm cache
ashley: can we rollback to 11.x image? dedicated pools can't all be drained without affecting customers
kevin: for dedicated we can route new requests to other regions; but customers in eu-west can't be moved due to latency SLAs
jia: cost note — autoscaler spun up 4 p3-equivalent instances, billed at on-demand; estimated extra cost ~$6k/day if we keep fallback for >24h
andre: proposed mitigation steps:
1) cordon + drain worst nodes: `kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
2) re-tag images with `cuda-toolkit:12.0-gcc11-compat` after rebuilding with libstdc++ compatible libs
3) enable canary rollback for the pool via deploy-bot
4) temporarily set `CUDA_CACHE_MAX_SIZE=0` to avoid PTX write storm
ashley: starting step1 now, will open PR for rebuild images
kevin: also add `--device=/dev/nvidiactl` hostPath to prevent missing kernel module errors (short-term hack)
andre: long term: we need node AMI that includes compatible drivers + GCC toolchain or switch to static linking of runtime libs
jia: agree. can we add a preflight check in CI to detect host driver vs image ABI mismatch? failing fast avoids this
ashley: oncall: if we hit >5% error budget in next 2h we'll trigger cross-region fallback. I'll post updates
sre-rotations: noted. tagging infra postmortem channel when stabilized
ashley: update: drained 7 nodes, rebuilt 2 canary images with gcc11 toolchain, canary smoke passed. still monitoring PTX cache IO. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
kevin: noted, I'm throttling kube-scheduler's pod burst to limit reschedules (kube-apiserver patch applied)
andre: leaving a TODO: add kernel module probe at boot and add alert for `modprobe nvidia` failures
oncall-bot: incident severity set to Sev2 — follow incident runbook
ashley: final note — avoid forcing toolkit upgrade across entire fleet; use staged rollout with canary + image ABI validation
